statement: The unit quaternion (versor) U q of a non-zero quaternion q is a quaternion with unit norm (||U q|| = 1) occupying the unit 3-sphere in H, derived from q by expressing it in Hamilton's polar coordinate form q = T q U q = ||q|| U q and normalizing q by its norm to yield U q = q / ||q||.

symbols.meaning: Hamilton's tensor (norm) of q, equal to ||q||
algebraic imaginary unit vector with r^2 = -1

steps.text: Display a general quaternion q in polar coordinate form as the product of its norm (Hamilton's tensor T q = ||q||) and its versor U q: q = T q U q = ||q|| U q.

Normalize the quaternion q by dividing by its non-zero norm T q = ||q|| to isolate the unit quaternion (versor): U q = q / (T q) = q / ||q||, which satisfies ||U q|| = 1 and occupies the unit 3-sphere in the quaternion algebra H.

assumptions.assumption: The quaternion q is non-zero (q != 0, so ||q|| > 0).
assumptions.breaks_when: q = 0, where the norm ||q|| = 0 and normalization involves division by zero, leaving the versor undefined.

assumptions.assumption: The quaternion q is an element of the four-dimensional quaternion algebra H equipped with norm T q = ||q||.
assumptions.breaks_when: The algebra lacks a well-defined norm or non-zero elements lack multiplicative inverses.

failure_modes.signature: Division by zero or undefined versor U q (indeterminate form 0/0).
failure_modes.cause: Attempting to normalize the zero quaternion q = 0, whose norm T q = ||q|| = 0 lacks a multiplicative inverse.
